idiom_name: Apache Camel intercept / interceptFrom toggled from the Control Bus
implementation_notes: Camel leaves the primary route untouched and inserts the detour with intercept()/interceptFrom(), guarded by an onWhen predicate that reads a control header or exchange property, so the extra step (audit bean, validator, fault injector) runs only while the switch is on and the exchange then continues to the original destination endpoints. The switch itself travels on the Control Bus - controlbus:route?routeId=...&action=suspend|resume|start|stop - which is exactly the EIP pairing of Detour with Control Bus. Note that interceptFrom is not dynamic: it binds the routes known at start-up, so per-endpoint interception of runtime-constructed URIs needs interceptSendToEndpoint.
pitfalls: A global intercept() fires before every processing step, so enabling it for one message class silently multiplies the work per exchange.
interceptFrom binds only routes known at start-up; a route created at runtime never sees it.
The control-bus endpoint can suspend, resume or stop live routes, so it must be secured and audited - Camel's Control Bus component is a management surface, not an application channel.

variants.name: Spring Integration control-bus command + switchable router
variants.idiom_name: ControlBusFactoryBean command endpoint + router on a managed flag
variants.implementation_notes: Spring Integration exposes the toggle as messages: a control-bus endpoint invokes @ManagedOperation/@ManagedAttribute methods on a bean, and the detour is a router whose output channel mapping is bound to that bean's managed flag. The primary flow definition is never touched - the operator sends a command such as 'auditToggle.enable' on the control channel, and the router switches the message between the audit sub-flow and the direct channel to the same destination. The Spring Integration reference explicitly recommends securing control-bus message reception because the commands can change system state.
pitfalls: Without @ManagedOperation/@ManagedAttribute (or a Lifecycle/Pausable method) the bean is not eligible as a control-bus command, and the toggle appears to do nothing.
Control-bus reception must be secured and exposed only where it belongs - the commands can suspend, resume or stop live components.
